tier1.text: Each pectoralis major crosses the shoulder joint to move the humerus, the upper arm bone. The pectoralis major adducts the arm, drawing it toward or across the middle of the body. This thick, fan-shaped muscle covers much of the upper front of the chest. The pectoralis major is a convergent muscle: its fiber bundles spread wide, then meet in a tendon on the humerus.

quotes.quote: The term may refer to one of two muscles, the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor. The former is a thick muscle in the anterior portion of the chest. Its action involves flexion, medial rotation, and adduction of the humerus.
quotes.citation: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), National Cancer Institute, https://ncithesaurus.nci.nih.gov

quotes.quote: adduction: movement in the coronal plane that moves a limb medially toward or across the midline of the body
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The large muscle on the chest, the pectoralis major, is an example of a convergent muscle because it converges on the greater tubercle of the humerus via a tendon.

quotes.quote: convergent: fascicles that extend over a broad area and converge on a common attachment site
